title: Sultanate of Sukadana
capsule: The Sultanate of Sukadana was a Muslim polity on the southwestern coast of Borneo (modern Ketapang Regency, West Kalimantan) that emerged from the earlier Tanjungpura Kingdom when the capital relocated to Sukadana; Islam spread through the realm around 1550 under Pangeran Giri Kesuma. The sultanate engaged in active trade in forest products, diamonds, and pepper, drawing Dutch and English commercial competition from the early 17th century; the VOC conducted military operations against its rulers and the polity came under increasing Dutch suzerainty after the fall of Makassar in 1667. Over the 18th and early 19th centuries the sultans retained nominal authority while Dutch colonial administration tightened, and by the mid-19th century Sukadana's functions were absorbed into the broader framework of Dutch Borneo governance.

Documentation for the Sultanate of Sukadana is fragmentary, relying on Dutch VOC records and local Malay chronicles; territorial boundaries are not precisely established.
